provenance.subject: dino
provenance.prompt:
Generate an image for a video game using the following art brief.

PROJECT ART DIRECTION
World: No Internet — Painted Dream
Style: Original luminous gouache and colored-pencil storybook illustration, visible velvety brush texture and torn-paper edges, rounded organic silhouettes, NOT pixel art, NOT blocky voxel or low polygon. Lighthearted surreal Mesozoic garden. All subjects have coherent cool turquoise shadows, coral peach highlights and rich cream sunlit rims. Soft painted dimensional forms, crisp isolated silhouettes readable at small game scale.
Palette: Jade/teal dinosaur, apricot/coral mushrooms, pale warm peach sky, deep aubergine-violet shadows, cream edges, small golden-yellow dorsal plates.
Constraints: Original designs only; no franchise imitation, no trademarks, no text, no watermarks, no drop shadows on isolated sprites. Deliver actual image using image-generation tool, not an SVG, code, or instructions. True transparent alpha when requested; never draw checkerboard. All objects fully in frame with generous padding.

OUTPUT PRESET
Full-body game character sprite. Entire body visible, consistent viewpoint, centered with padding.

COMPOSITION OPTIONS
Aspect: square
View: three-quarter
Background: transparent
Rendering detail: painted
Additional notes: Game sprite animation atlas, exactly 2 columns by 2 rows, four equal square cells, no grid lines. Consistent elevated REAR three-quarter view: camera follows dinosaur from behind and slightly its left; dinosaur runs away toward upper-right of canvas, see its back, left cheek/eye, tail points down-left. Same size, angle, baseline and identity in all cells. Transparent space around each figure. Feet baseline at 85% of each cell. No ground/no shadows/no scene.

CANONICAL ASSET DEFINITIONS
CHARACTER: Painted dream runner dinosaur
One original friendly small Tyrannosaurus: jade teal body, cream belly and chin, exactly three golden-yellow dorsal plates along its back, short rounded snout, bright small eye, two tiny arms, sturdy hind legs, thick curved balancing tail. Preserve shape and proportions. Illustrated gouache with organic curves and visible painterly texture.

REFERENCE ROLES
No images attached.

PRESERVE
Preserve approved character identity, proportions, signature details and selected outfit/prop designs. Identity references control character identity. Style references control rendering, not character identity. Environment references control setting, not character anatomy.

REQUESTED CHANGE / COMPOSITION
Generate ONE square PNG sprite atlas with four consistent full-body poses of the same dinosaur. Top-left: run pose A, left hind foot forward. Top-right: run pose B, right hind foot forward. Bottom-left: airborne jumping pose, legs tucked slightly, whole dinosaur raised a little without cropping tail. Bottom-right: neutral standing pose. Every cell shows same full dinosaur facing AWAY toward upper right in elevated rear three-quarter view, suitable for a behind-runner camera. Smooth readable silhouette, round organic anatomy, painterly shading, jade body/cream belly/3gold dorsal plates. Exactly four characters, one in each quadrant. Large transparent gutters. Do not include labels. Actual generated image.

OUTPUT
Generate the image, not just a description. No captions, labels, watermarks or extra objects unless requested. Transparency, exact dimensions and game readiness will be validated separately.

FINAL CONTINUITY CONTRACT (highest priority for visual continuity)
This is a general continuity generation. The brief may change angle, pose, expression, clothing, or lighting, but must not redesign the pinned identity or location.
PRESERVE: character identity, apparent age, hair, facial structure, and body proportions; reviewed definitions and approved world style.
ALLOWED CHANGES: Changes explicitly requested by the composition brief, where compatible with continuity..
The pinned original is the visual authority for face, hair, body proportions, silhouette, floor plan, materials, and landmarks. Reviewed text fills in nonvisual details and world rules; it must not quietly redesign visible identity or layout.
If a manual original appears to disagree with reviewed text, preserve its visible continuity and flag the result for human review rather than claiming automated visual verification.
Never invent a new face. Do not claim pixel identity: generative output can drift, so human visual review is still required.
